Name: viral membrane
The lipid bilayer of a virion, a complete fully infectious extracellular virus particle.

Name: host cell plasma membrane
The plasma membrane surrounding a host cell.

Name: AP-2 adaptor complex
A heterotetrameric AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex that consists of alpha, beta2, mu2 and sigma2 subunits, and links clathrin to the membrane surface of a vesicle, and the cargo receptors during receptor/clathrin mediated endocytosis. Vesicles with AP-2-containing coats are normally found primarily near the plasma membrane, on endocytic vesicles. In at least humans, the AP-2 complex can be heterogeneric due to the existence of multiple subunit isoforms encoded by different alpha genes (alphaA and alphaC).

Name: cytoplasm
All of the contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.

Name: virion
The complete fully infectious extracellular virus particle. Any constituent part of a virion, a complete fully infectious extracellular virus particle.

Name: virion
The complete fully infectious extracellular virus particle. Any constituent part of a virion, a complete fully infectious extracellular virus particle.

Name: endosome
A vacuole to which materials ingested by endocytosis are delivered. An transient hybrid organelle formed by fusion of a late endosome with a lysosome, and in which active degradation takes place.

Name: extracellular region
The space external to the outermost structure of a cell. For cells without external protective or external encapsulating structures this refers to space outside of the plasma membrane. This term covers the host cell environment outside an intracellular parasite.

Name: fusion of virus membrane with host plasma membrane
Fusion of a viral membrane with the host cell membrane during viral entry. Results in release of the virion contents into the cytoplasm. The plasma membrane surrounding a host cell.

Name: nucleus
A membrane-bounded organelle of eukaryotic cells in which chromosomes are housed and replicated. In most cells, the nucleus contains all of the cell's chromosomes except the organellar chromosomes, and is the site of RNA synthesis and processing. In some species, or in specialized cell types, RNA metabolism or DNA replication may be absent.

Name: viral nucleocapsid
The complete protein-nucleic acid complex that is the packaged form of the genome in a virus particle.

Name: clathrin-dependent endocytosis Charge: 0
An endocytosis process that begins when material is taken up into clathrin-coated pits, which then pinch off to form clathrin-coated endocytic vesicles.

Name: symbiont entry into host cell Charge: 0
The process by which a symbiont breaches the plasma membrane or cell envelope and enters the host cell. The process ends when the symbiont or its genome is released into the host cell.

Name: proteasome-mediated ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process
The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein or peptide by hydrolysis of its peptide bonds, initiated by the covalent attachment of ubiquitin, and mediated by the proteasome.
